sentence: This project studies a kinase pathway in high-grade gliomas of children, using cell lines and mouse models to design drugs that target these tumors.
This project tries to reprogram cardiac fibroblast signaling pathways toward a cardiogenic genetic network, using a CRISPR-based pathway editor to target fibrosis after myocardial injury.
This project studies how immune cells work together in tissues to make antibodies during inflammatory conditions, and how this could help treat and prevent cancer.
This project studies how the protein Poldip2 controls endothelial cell permeability, which can lead to tissue edema and inflammation.
This project builds optical simulation software with AI to help develop fast radiation detectors for nuclear imaging.
This project builds two human cell culture models of a fatal childhood neurodegenerative disorder, using cells from individuals with the disorder, to help test treatments.
This project studies brain network changes in a rat model of epilepsy after brain injury, to predict who will develop the disease.
This project compares fluorescent proteins against each other in Caenorhabditis elegans to see how well they work in living animals.
This project builds gold nanoprobes that make luminescence without oxygen, to detect and monitor hypoxic tumors.
This project builds an artificial intelligence framework that lets a robotic exoskeleton or prosthesis adapt to the walking pattern of each patient.
This project studies how benzoic acid, nicotine and nicotine benzoate in electronic cigarettes affect fetal lungs during pregnancy.
This project provides bioinformatics and biostatistical support for prostate cancer research projects.
This project tests how biochemical pathways respond to changes in nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide and looks for alternative forms of vitamin B3.
This project builds a cellular atlas of human head and neck cancer to find how cellular communication drives tumor progression.
This project studies the function of a factor that regulates mitochondrial signaling and is required for cardiac health.
This project provides mouse models and monoclonal antibodies to help researchers study peroxisomes and peroxisomal disorders.
This project studies how and when the shape, localization and function of mitochondria affect oligodendrocyte development, death and regeneration in the live brain.
This project studies how smoking withdrawal changes the way the brain processes pain, and whether this makes it harder to stop smoking.
This project studies how manganese exposure changes neurotransmission and promotes tau pathology in a transgenic mouse model of Alzheimer’s disease.
This project builds data resources and tools that help researchers test links from genetic, molecular and cellular traits to behaviors related to substance use disorders.
